findings.title: remove_transition ignores State/Enum members inside a list for source/dest
findings.property: removing with source=[State] (or dest=[State]) removes exactly the same transitions as passing the state name strings
findings.input: Machine(states=['A','B','C'], auto_transitions=False); add_transition('go','A','B'); add_transition('go','B','C'); remove_transition('go', source=[m.get_state('A')])
findings.actual: nothing is removed; both transitions remain
findings.evidence: Docstring: source/dest are 'str, Enum or State'; the code listify()s the argument and converts each element, but the comprehension tests hasattr(source, 'name') (the whole list/original arg) instead of hasattr(s, 'name'), so list elements that are State/Enum are never converted to names and never match t.source/t.dest (stored as names). The same State passed alone (not in a list) works.

review.title: remove_transition does not convert State/Enum elements in a source/dest list to names
review.reason: In core.py:1141 and 1143 the comprehensions test `hasattr(source, 'name')` and `hasattr(dest, 'name')` on the whole argument instead of the loop variable `s`/`d`. After `listify`, a list of State or Enum objects therefore keeps its elements unconverted and never matches `t.source`/`t.dest`, which are stored as names. A single State passed alone works because `listify` wraps it and the whole-argument check happens to see `.name`. The repro is valid and fails deterministically, and the fix is a one-token change that a maintainer would accept. The only doubt is that the docstring says `str, Enum or State` and doesn't explicitly mention lists, but the code runs `listify` and a list of names works, so lists are clearly intended.

findings.reproSource:
from transitions import Machine


def test_repro_remove_transition_list_of_state_objects():
    m = Machine(states=['A', 'B', 'C'], initial='A', auto_transitions=False)
    m.add_transition('go', 'A', 'B')
    m.add_transition('go', 'B', 'C')
    m.remove_transition('go', source=[m.get_state('A')])
    assert [(t.source, t.dest) for t in m.get_transitions('go')] == [('B', 'C')]
